findings: Scattered small microaneurysms detected in the temporal retina outside the avascular zone
Focal mild venous tortuosity along the inferior vascular branch
Rare tiny punctate dot hemorrhage near the superior temporal arcade
No cotton wool spots, hard exudates, or neovascularization detected in visible field
maculaStatus: Foveal reflex intact; no hard exudates or macular thickening observed.
opticDiscStatus: Normal disc appearance with sharp margins and cup-to-disc ratio of 0.35.
riskIndicators: Low to moderate risk of progression within 12 months under good metabolic control
Routine semi-annual or annual monitoring recommended
recommendation: Routine ophthalmology follow-up recommended within 6 to 12 months.
analysisSummary: AI visual screening indicates mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) characterized by sparse microaneurysms and mild vascular tortuosity. No maculopathy or high-risk features were identified. Systemic control optimization and routine follow-up are advised.
differentialConsiderations: Early hypertensive microangiopathy considered due to vessel tortuosity; mild NPDR remains primary diagnosis.
